subject: How does shiny manage the state?

messages.author: a721db0167550d24
messages.subject: How does shiny manage the state?
parts:
Hello,

I am new to R and shiny, both. I really like the way, shiny allows users to create the web UI's from R code. I was curious to know how R manages the state (reactive variables and other entities). The code for renderPlot shows a reference to "shinysession". Does this session hold cached values? I am just trying to understand shiny architecture better. In the eventReactive example available as part of the webinar, when the slider is moved, its current value is sent to the server and it then gets used later when the button is pressed. Where is the previous slider value stored?

What recommendations do shiny users have to write an application that supports fail over? Also, is there any way to debug a built-in shiny function like renderPlot?

Thanks
Sachin

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: How does shiny manage the state?
parts:
The eventReactive object caches its own value, effectively. The same is true of reactive(). The session object holds current copies of the user input but not too much else in terms of what's necessary for calculations. (I'm not sure how to shine light on how Shiny is implemented, it's quite a big topic and I'm still trying to figure out if knowing the implementation actually helps people write better apps.)

You can debug using debug(renderPlot), then running your app. It helps to install shiny with "R CMD INSTALL --with-keep.source shiny" (where shiny is the path to the shiny github project on your local disk).

For fail over you can use shiny server like any other webserver--put two or more behind a proxy or load balancer that supports fail over. If a server goes down you will lose existing sessions (due to the stateful nature of Shiny that's a bit tricky to solve) but future sessions will go to the new server.
